Reductions with diimide:
- Isolated carbon-carbon double bonds can be reduced with hydrazine \(\left(\mathrm{NH}_2 \mathrm{NH}_2\right)\) in the presence of oxygen or an oxidizing agent.
- The actual reducing agent in these reactions is the highly active species diimide, \(\mathrm{HN}=\mathrm{NH}\), formed in situ by oxidation of hydrazine.
- This compound is a highly selective reducing agent which in many cases offers a useful alternative to catalytic hydrogenation for the reduction of carbon-carbon multiple bonds.
- The reagent diimide is prepared by oxidation of hydrazine, by decomposition of tosylhydrazide, or from azodicarboxylic acid.
- It is a suitable reducing agent for symmetrical double bonds such as \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\), and \(\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}\), but unsymmetrical, more polar bonds such as \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{N}=\mathrm{O}\), and \(\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{O}\) are not reduced. questions.q: Which of the following has maximum dipole moment?
questions.solution:
Electronegativity difference between $\mathrm{N}(3.0)$ and $\mathrm{Cl}(3.0)$ is zero and hence, $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bonds are non-polar. As a result, the overall dipole moment of $\mathrm{NCl}_3$ molecule and its direction is just the dipole moment of the lone pair of electrons.
On the other hand, $\mathrm{N}-\operatorname{Br}(3.0-2.8)$, $\mathrm{N}-1(3.0-2.5)$ and $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}(3.0-2.1)$ are polar and hence, contribute towards the overall dipole moment of the respective molecules. Since the EN difference is highest in case of $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds, therefore, $\mathrm{NH}_3$ has the highest dipole moment.

$ \begin{aligned}

 & =\frac{n(n+1)}{4}\left(n^2+n-2\right) \\

Magnetic field density $B$ due to long straight current carrying conductor at a distance $r$ is given as
$B=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi} \cdot \frac{i}{r}$
i.e.
$B \propto \frac{1}{r}$
Hence, option (3) is correct.

questions.q: A solenoid of length 0.4 m and having 500 turns of wire carries a current of $3 \mathrm{~A}$. A thin coil having 10 , turns of wire and of radius 0.01 m carries a current of 0.4 A. The torque required to hold the coil in the middle of the solenoid with its axis perpendicular to the axis of solenoid.
questions.solution:
Magnetic field inside the solenoid,
$\begin{aligned} B & =\mu_0 n l \\ & =\mu_0 \frac{N}{1} \cdot 1 \\ \Rightarrow B & =4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times \frac{500}{0.4} \times 3\end{aligned}\therefore$ Torque,
$\begin{aligned} \tau= & I A B N \\ = & 3 \times\left(\pi r^2\right) \times\left(\frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 500 \times 3}{0.4}\right) \times 500 \\ = & 3 \times \frac{22}{7} \times\left(0.01 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & \times \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 500 \times 3}{0.4} \times 500 \\ = & 5.92 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A short bar magnet of magnetic moment of $0.15 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{T}$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T . The potential energy of the magnet in unstable equilibrium is
questions.solution:
Magnetic potential of a bar magnet in external magnetic field is given by
$U=-M B \cos \theta$
Here, $M=0.15 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{T}, B=0.4 \mathrm{~T}$,
and $\theta=180^{\circ}$ as magnet is in unstable equilibrium.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad U & =-0.15 \times 0.4 \times \cos 180^{\circ} \\ & =-0.15 \times 0.4 \times(-1) \\ & =6 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

$F_2=1350 \mathrm{~kg}=1350 \times 9.8 \mathrm{~N}, r_2=\frac{10}{100} \mathrm{~m}$
According to Pascal law, As, $\frac{F_1}{A_1}=\frac{F_2}{A_2}$ or $F_1=\frac{A_1}{A_2} F_2=\frac{\pi r_1^2}{\pi r_2^2} F_2$

questions.q: The potential energy of a particle of mass 0.1 kg moving along the $X$-axis, is given by $U=5 x(x-4) \mathrm{J}$, where $x$ is in metres. Choose the wrong option.
options: The speed of the particle is maximum at $x=2 \mathrm{~m}$
The particle executes simple harmonic motion
The period of oscillation of the particle is $\frac{\pi}{5} \mathrm{~s}$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & U=5 x^2-20 x, \frac{d U}{d x}=10 x-20 \\ & F=-\frac{d U}{d x}=(-10 x+20)\end{aligned}$
Let us suppose, $x=(X+2)$. Then, $F=-10 X$, $F=0$ at $X=0$ or $x=2$, i.e. $x=2 \mathrm{~m}$ is the mean position about which particle is in SHM. $k=10\therefore T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{0.1}{10}}=\frac{\pi}{5} \mathrm{~s}$
At mean position kinetic energy is maximum and force acting on particle in SHM is variable.

questions.q:
A light ray of wavelength 546 nm is incident on an air-glass interface. If the speed of light in air is $3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Then, wavelength of light ray in glass will be
[Take, refractive index of glass, $\mu=1.5$ ]
questions.solution:
Given, wavelength of light,
$\lambda=546 \mathrm{~nm}$
Refractive ve index, $\mu=1.5$
Speed of light, $c=3 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$
Refractive index,
$\begin{aligned} \mu & =\frac{\text { Speed of light in vacuum (c) }}{\text { Speed of light in glass (v) }} \\ & =\frac{c}{v} \\ & =\frac{v \lambda}{v \lambda_g}\left[\lambda_g=\text { wavelength of light in glass }\right] \\ \mu & =\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_g} \Rightarrow \lambda_g=\frac{\lambda}{\mu} \\ & =\frac{546}{1.5}=364 \mathrm{~nm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A cyclic process for 1 mole of an ideal is shown in the $V-T$ diagram. The work done in $A B, B C$ and $C A$ respectively is
questions.solution:
Process $A B$ is isochoric, hence $W_{A B}=0$
Process $B C$ is isothermal, hence
$W_{B C}=n R T_2 \ln \left(\frac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$
or $\quad W_{B C}=R T_2 \ln \left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)$
Process $C A$ is isobaric (as, $V \propto T)\therefore W_{C A}=p\left(V_f-V_i\right)=n R\left(T_t-T_i\right)=R\left(T_1-T_2\right)$

questions.q: Imagine a system of unit in which the unit of mass is 10 kg , length is 1 km and time is 1 min . Then, 1 J in this system is equal to
questions.solution:
As joule is the SI unit of energy and dimensional formula for energy is $\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$. In this question, we have to convert one unit into another, therefore
$\begin{aligned} \eta_1\left[M_1 L_1^2 T_1^{-2}\right] & =\eta_2\left[M_2 L_2^2 T_2^{-2}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \quad \eta_2 & =\eta_1\left[\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right]^1\left[\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right]^2\left[\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right]^{-2} \\ & =1 \times\left[\frac{1 \mathrm{~kg}}{10 \mathrm{~kg}}\right]^1\left[\frac{1 \mathrm{~m}}{1 \mathrm{~km}}\right]^2\left[\frac{1 \mathrm{~s}}{1 \mathrm{~min}}\right]^{-2} \\ & =1 \times\left[\frac{1 \mathrm{~kg}}{10 \mathrm{~kg}}\right]^1\left[\frac{1 \mathrm{~m}}{10^3 \mathrm{~m}}\right]^2\left[\frac{1 \mathrm{~s}}{60 \mathrm{~s}}\right]^{-2} \\ & =1 \times 10^{-1} \times 10^{-6} \times 36 \times 10^2 \\ \eta_2 & =36 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The work done in moving a charge particle of charge $2 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C}$ between two points having potential difference of 36 V is
questions.solution: Given, $q=2 \times 10^{-8}, \Delta V=36 \mathrm{~V}\begin{aligned}\textrm{Work done,} W & =q \cdot \Delta V \\ & =2 \times 10^{-8} \times 36 \\ & =72 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~V} \\ & =0.72 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~V} \\ & =0.72 \mu \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$
